messages:
Incident Bot: :rotating_light: Pager: inference-api.canary p95 latency spike & elevated 5xx rate. 4 triggers in 2m. runbook: https://redwood/internal/runbooks/inference-canary
Sam: Oncall here. What changed in the canary?
Mira: Rolling out canary for the new kv-cache-change FF (canary bucket). Saw p95 jump from ~120ms -> 900ms and 5xx from 0.1% -> 1.8%.
Nate: Noticed a pattern: cache miss storm when the new cache path hits a fallback codepath that allocates extra CPU. Might be thundering herd from cold shards.
Sam: Any dashboard showing canary vs stable? I'm not seeing separate dashboard panels for the canary tag in the main dashboards.
Mira: Yeah that's the issue — we forgot to include rollout_id tagging in the canary telemetry. Metrics are aggregated across both, so alerts fire but we can't isolate.
Priya: Oof. So alerts are noisy and we can't tell if stable is affected. Customer impact?
Mira: Early look: Dedicated customers on the canary pool experienced token latency spikes and a small increase in 5xx. Logged customer errors show ~1200 failed requests in last 10m, mostly timeouts (upstream grpc deadline exceeded).
Sam: @Deploy Bot, can you show the canary commit and the feature flag toggle?
Deploy Bot: Canary deploy info: commit abc123 -> image redwood/inference:canary-2026-03-15
Deploy Bot: Feature flag: canary_new_cache = enabled for rollout_id=roll_42 (10% of traffic)
Sam: Immediate mitigation options?
Nate: We can kill the FF (fast) or roll back the canary (slower, but safer if stateful). Kill-FF is risky if rollback logic not exercised.
Mira: Given telemetry blindspot, we should kill the flag to stop the new path immediately. Then we can confirm stable metrics.
Sam: Do it. Post the command you will run.
Nate: Running kill switch now:
```
# internal flag service
curl -XPOST -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  https://flags.internal/api/v1/flags/canary_new_cache/kill \
  -d '{"environment":"prod","rollout_id":"roll_42"}'
```
Nate: Response: {"status":"ok","disabled":true} :white_check_mark:
Mira: Kill worked. Starting to see p95 drop on the canary host group within one minute. 5xx rate falling back toward baseline.
Sam: Confirming stable pool metrics: p95 unchanged, 5xx baseline. Good.
Priya: Customer impact assessment: 7 customers in canary pool saw degraded UX. No widespread outage. We should notify Customer Success with the list and timeline.
Lee: Noted observability gaps: 1) rollout_id not emitted on metrics 2) no dedicated canary dashboard panels 3) alert rules not scoped by rollout_id, so on-call had to triage blind.
Sam: Agreed. Immediate action items: kill flag (done), notify CS (Priya), open postmortem and add runbook step to verify telemetry tags before rollout (me), hotfix: add rollout_id tag to metrics pipeline (Mira/Nate).
Priya: I'll ping CS and draft a short customer update.
Mira: For the hotfix, we can push a small telemetry sidecar bump that tags metrics on ingress. Will try to get PR by EOD.
Nate: Also propose a pre-rollout checklist entry: "Canary telemetry visibility — ensure dedicated panels and tag filters present."
Sam: Assigning postmortem to @Mira and @Nate, with me as reviewer. Priya will coordinate CS comms.
Deploy Bot: Recording incident: INC-2026-045. Severity: S2. Timeline: 2056789012 - 2056789145
Sam: Thanks all. Follow-up: add canary-specific dashboards, scope alerts by rollout_id, and create automation to disable FF if p95 > 2x baseline within 2m.
Mira: Adding owners in the ticket. Also adding a telemetry test to our CI to ensure rollout_id present for any canary deploy.
Lee: Note for postmortem: quantify customer impact (requests affected, error types), and timeline of detection vs mitigation.
Priya: CS informed, short blurb sent to affected accounts, offering help and an incident summary.
Sam: Closing thread for now — watch for any regression and update INC ticket with the postmortem link when ready. :thumbsup:
